assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of a boson at about 125 GeV completed the Standard Model and was a clear experimental discovery of a long-predicted particle. The 2013 prize recognised the theory; the measurement itself has not been recognised and is a discovery in the plainest sense.
assessment.attribution: The discovery was made by two collaborations of thousands. Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are widely credited as founding leaders of CMS and ATLAS (and of the detector concepts), which gives a defensible three-person configuration, but this is institutional leadership credit and not discovery-day credit.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation by two experiments, later coupling and spin-parity measurements, and more than a decade of stability make recognition fully mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the Academy accepts leadership of large collaborations as the decisive contribution is a policy question, not a scientific one.
Credit for the analyses that actually produced the 2012 signal rests with many people outside this trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are direct, visual evidence for the near-horizon geometry of black holes and constrain deviations from general relativity. They are a striking empirical anchor for quantum-gravity-minded theorists, though the 2020 prize already honoured black-hole existence.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the VLBI array development and the collaboration, and Zensus built the European mm-VLBI infrastructure. The collaboration is large and the credit is diffuse, but this trio is a plausible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Two independent sources imaged, polarisation results and consistent mass measurements. Interpretation of the ring as a shadow is stable, though tests of strong-field gravity remain model-dependent.
uncertainties: Priority between concept originators, instrument builders and image-reconstruction teams is contested.
Overlap with the 2020 prize may make the committee cautious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks with magic-wavelength trapping reach about 1e-18 fractional uncertainty, redefining precision timekeeping and enabling tests of fundamental constants and relativistic redshift at millimetre scales. The idea is original and the experimental impact is clear and measurable.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and Ye achieved the leading demonstrations and accuracy records. A two-person configuration is clean. Other contributors (e.g. ion-clock and comb work) were already recognised in 2005 and 2012.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs reproduce and compare clocks at the 1e-18 level; the redefinition of the second is under discussion. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Some may argue the Hall-Haensch and Wineland prizes already cover much of the territory.
Early lattice-clock proposals had additional contributors that I cannot verify in detail.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators opened a new class of matter, connecting band topology to measurable edge transport. Theory plus rapid experimental confirmation make this a model case of a discovery with lasting impact across condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 invariant and quantum spin Hall state in graphene; Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe quantum wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Zhang, Fu, Moore and Hasan also made decisive contributions, so a three-person selection leaves out important parties.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed in several materials, including ARPES studies of 3D topological insulators; the field is mature and the 2016 prize covered only topological phase transitions.
uncertainties: Unresolved allocation of credit between theory proposals (Kane-Mele, BHZ) and 3D topological insulators, and the exclusion of Zhang, who is deceased.
Not all of these names are in the supplied credited list, so the configuration is constrained.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity founded the field of moire quantum materials, with a very rapid and large impact on condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group did the 2018 experiments. The theory-experiment pairing is clean and a three-person prize is natural.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have replicated the phases, though the nature of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still debated. It is early (about 8 years) but the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: Interpretation of the superconducting mechanism is unsettled.
The Cao-Jarillo-Herrero experiment shares credit with coauthors not on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP gave the first precision determination of cosmological parameters from the CMB, establishing LambdaCDM with percent-level constraints on age, geometry, baryon and dark matter content and showing near scale invariance. It is foundational for modern cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was a key instrument scientist, and Spergel led the cosmological analysis. This is a defensible trio, but the Planck team and the earlier COBE/BOOMERanG/Wilkinson lineage also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed and superseded by Planck, so the results are stable; the timing is late, and the 2006 and 2019 prizes already honoured major parts of CMB cosmology.
uncertainties: Whether a mission-leadership prize adds enough to the 2006 COBE prize.
The Hubble tension complicates the long-term interpretation without undermining WMAP itself.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: AdS/CFT is among the most influential ideas in theoretical physics, linking gravity and gauge theory and shaping work on black-hole information, QCD plasmas and strongly correlated matter. As a string theorist I recognise its depth, but a Nobel prize needs clues from nature and the duality has no direct experimental test of its core claim.
assessment.attribution: Maldacena proposed the duality in 1997, and Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov and Witten supplied the dictionary. 't Hooft and Susskind contributed the holographic principle. A three-person prize is possible but leaves a contested allocation.
assessment.maturity: Extensively checked by consistency and integrability, with applications to heavy-ion and condensed-matter systems, but no direct empirical confirmation of gravity duals; recognition may be premature for the committee.
uncertainties: No decisive experimental test of the duality.
Credit between Maldacena, Gubser, Klebanov, Polyakov, Witten, 't Hooft and Susskind is contested and Gubser and Klebanov are not in the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Stable numerical evolution of binary black-hole mergers in 2005 (Pretorius) and the moving-puncture methods in 2006 (Campanelli et al., Baker et al.) made the waveform templates used in gravitational-wave discovery possible. The impact is large but sits downstream of the 2017 LIGO prize.
assessment.attribution: Pretorius achieved the first breakthrough; the two moving-puncture groups independently found a second route. This is an unusually clean three-way credit statement, though other numerical-relativity contributors (e.g. Thornburg, Bruegmann) are not in the list.
assessment.maturity: The methods are universally adopted and validated against observed signals, so confirmation is excellent; the question is whether a methods prize is wanted after 2017.
uncertainties: Whether numerical relativity is viewed as computational technique versus fundamental physics.
Attribution between the Pretorius, UTB and Goddard teams is not wholly settled.
